text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Editorial says Albania is in a difficult historical moment and the future in the new millennium will depend on how it is solved.
- An front-page commentary says the Voice of America radio station has lost credibility because its staff in Albania is very partial in favour of the ruling party.
- The Forum for Democracy opposition coalition is to stage a mass protest in Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square on Saturday.
- Depositors of the bankrupt Gjallica investment scheme in the southern town of Vlore held the second successive day of protests blaming the government for its collapse.
- The Forum for Democracy asks for a meeting with President Sali Berisha and to organise a demonstration to support the protest in Vlore.
- U.S. State Department calls on Albanians to solve their problems in a peaceful way. A political, constructive dialogue would serve the future democratic stability in Albania.
- Commentary says the government is threatened with a "Belgrade" phenomenon with Vlore as a starting point.
- Azem Hajdari, a founder of the ruling Democratic Party and currently leader of a trade union and a member of parliament, said Vlore cannot be controlled with the army.
- Pjeter Arbnori, speaker of the parliament, interrupted a discussion on Vlore, saying it was not in the day's agenda.
- A trade union in the capital Tirana issues a petition demanding the government's resignation and the complete refunding of depositors' money.
- Chaos surrounds the distribution of partial refunds of frozen funds of two failed pyramid investment scheme companies.
- Albanians around the country are asking for permission to hold peaceful meetings to denounce the government for the fall of pyramid schemes.
- Police started looking for Gjallica chief manager Shemsie Kadria, who has left the country.
